gen_text: Name, address and phone are mandatory strings; bank account is optional.
Given a new customer record with all mandatory fields, when the record is saved, then the system assigns a unique Customer-ID.
Each product has a name, description, price (decimal) and image URL.
Given a request for the product list, when the system returns the list, then every product includes all four attributes.
Order total = Σ (order-item.quantity × order-item.unit-price).
Given an Order with status submitted, when OrderStaff clicks Receive, then the Order status becomes pending.
The status transition submitted → pending is the only allowed transition from submitted.
Given an Order whose status is filled, when OrderStaff attempts to receive it, then the system rejects the request and leaves the status unchanged.
Given an Order with status pending, when OrderStaff selects Mark as Filled, then the Order status becomes filled.
Given an Order with status pending, when OrderStaff selects Decline, then the Order status becomes closed.
Transition filled → shipped is the only allowed transition from filled.
Given an Order with status pending, when OrderStaff attempts to ship, then the request is rejected and the status remains pending.
Only one Invoice may exist per Order.
Given an Order whose status is submitted, pending or closed, when Accountant tries to raise an Invoice, then the request is rejected.
Given a Payment whose status is failed, when Accountant attempts to confirm it, then the request is rejected and the status stays failed.
Given a Payment with status pending, when Accountant marks it failed, then the Payment status becomes failed; the Invoice status remains unchanged.
Given an Order with status shipped and a linked Invoice with status paid, when OrderStaff selects Close, then the Order status becomes closed.
Given a shipped Order whose Invoice is not paid, when OrderStaff attempts to close, then the request is rejected and the status stays shipped.
Order.status ∈ {submitted, pending, filled, shipped, closed}.
Invoice.status ∈ {issued, paid}.
Payment.status ∈ {pending, completed, failed}.
Product.price, OrderItem.unitPrice, Order.totalAmount, Invoice.amount, Payment.amount are of type decimal(12,2).
No monetary field may be null.
Every status transition creates an audit record (entity, oldStatus, newStatus, userId, timestamp).
No status transition is allowed from closed.
Given a closed Order, when any staff attempts to change its status, then the request is rejected.
Unauthenticated requests are logged and rejected 100 % of the time.
Only users with role Accountant may invoke the Confirm Payment or Reject Payment actions.
95 % of order submissions with ≤ 50 items shall complete within 2 seconds.
Availability shall be ≥ 99.5 % per calendar month, with scheduled maintenance announced ≥ 24 h in advance.
Bank account numbers are stored encrypted at rest.
Given a known Customer-ID, at least one order item and a valid payment method, when the order is submitted, then an Order is created with status submitted and the current date as order-date.
Given a successfully created Order, when the total is queried, then the returned total equals the calculated sum.
No transition is allowed from pending to any status other than filled or closed.
Decline is only permitted from pending.
Given an Invoice with status paid, when a Payment is submitted, then the system rejects the submission.
Closing is only allowed from shipped when the Invoice is paid.
All attributes except Customer.bankAccount are mandatory.
Given any monetary input, when it is persisted, then the stored value retains two fractional digits.
The Order entity becomes read‑only after reaching closed.
Every API call must contain a valid authentication token.
Given a non‑Accountant user attempting to confirm a payment, when the request is processed, then the system returns HTTP 403 Forbidden.
